topComments.author: dlinder
topComments.text: Token-passing networks were interesting for hard real time system analysis, as they featured deterministic access control instead of collision detection. jobs.text: I’m Chris, VP Engineering at Fazeshift. We’re nine engineers plus our Founder/CTO and me, and I’m hiring someone who can help us do more, better: increase both what we can build and the quality and sophistication of the software we build. Accounts receivable sounds boring until you look under the hood. It sits at the intersection of money, business relationships, software systems of various vintages, and a huge amount of repetitive human work. Instead of giving finance teams another dashboard to stare at, we’re building AI agents that actually do the work across billing, collections, payments, cash application, and the systems connecting them. We’ve grown revenue 12x since 2024, and eight unicorns now run AR on Fazeshift. A big part of what makes the engineering interesting is that we’re intentionally not the system of record. Our customers already run on ERPs, CRMs, banks, billing systems, payment processors, spreadsheets, and internal software, so we have to understand state across systems we don’t control, act safely in them, and recover when reality disagrees with what an API says should have happened. A timeout doesn’t necessarily mean a write failed. Webhooks can arrive late or twice. A payment may not contain enough information to identify an invoice. In those cases, blindly retrying can be exactly the wrong thing to do. We use coding agents heavily ourselves. Engineers use Conductor, stacked PRs, Linear, and multiple frontier models every day, with internal skills and tooling that let agents drive and validate our local development environment. We’re especially interested in engineers whose development workflow has already materially changed because of coding agents: people who are comfortable delegating meaningful work, keeping independent threads moving in parallel, debugging where agents get stuck, and improving the surrounding system when the workflow breaks down. But generated code is still your code . Judgment, debugging, systems thinking, taste, and understanding what actually shipped matter more here, not less. Our development style is roughly: design enough to find the shape of the problem, then build to learn. There’s a short distance here between noticing a problem, deciding what should happen, building it, and seeing the result in production with our customers. You’ll own meaningful problems from ambiguity through design, implementation, rollout, and production, and you’ll work directly with the people affected by what you build. We’re looking for 5+ years of professional experience, strong TypeScript/full-stack skills, solid systems judgment, and real production ownership. No fintech background needed. Failed events are retried after a delay while newer events continue processing. My initial approach uses a separate claim for each destination: Claim A → update A → claim B → update B However, if a process crashes after claiming A but before updating it, the claim remains. A retry then skips A even though its update never happened. I am considering storing the value and processed-event hashes together in one cell per destination. A single CAS would atomically update the value and record the event hash, eliminating the gap between claiming and updating. The drawback is unbounded growth of the processed-event history. Bounding it by time or count could remove an event hash before a delayed retry arrives, allowing the event to be applied again. Hash collisions could also incorrectly identify a new event as a duplicate. What is the recommended approach for bounding deduplication history while preserving correctness under out-of-order retries? Also, I understand that atomic updates within A and B separately would not make the two-store update atomic. If strict all-or-nothing updates across both stores are required, what additional mechanism is needed?

quantaArticles.author: John Pavlus

quantaArticles.title: How Do Fungi Keep the Planet Healthy?
quantaArticles.description: Evolutionary biologist Toby Kiers explains how fungal networks in soil trade nutrients with plants, help keep carbon underground, and strike bargains without having a brain.
quantaArticles.author: Steven Strogatz and Janna Levin

quantaArticles.description: A collision may have left these galaxies without dark matter. That spells trouble for alternative gravity theories.
quantaArticles.author: Robin George Andrews

quantaArticles.title: Is ‘Attention’ the Essence of Intelligence?
quantaArticles.description: A mathematical mechanism enables AI models to process language at scale, undergirding the current AI revolution. Our columnist asks: Why is attention the key?
quantaArticles.author: Natalie Wolchover

quantaArticles.title: How Does Life Unfold? A Landscape Metaphor Comes Into Its Own.
quantaArticles.description: C.H. Waddington’s powerful image of embryonic stem cells specializing on a rolling landscape has captivated biologists since the 1950s. Experimental data is finally confirming, and complicating, his visionary ideas.
quantaArticles.author: Philip Ball

infoqArticles.title: Zod Brings In-Process Schema Compilation and a 9x Cut in Memory Footprint
infoqArticles.description: Zod is a TypeScript-focused schema validation library that recently released versions 4.5 and 4.6. Key updates include schema compilation for faster data parsing, significant memory usage reductions, and new validation features. The library supports efficient validation processes and remains popular in the JavaScript ecosystem, achieving millions of downloads weekly. By Daniel Curtis
infoqArticles.author: Daniel Curtis

infoqArticles.title: Uber Automates Dependency Analysis Across Its Service Mesh
infoqArticles.description: Uber has developed an automated dependency analysis system that uses RPC middleware and production metrics to correlate caller and downstream failures. The approach classifies dependencies as fail-close, fail-open, or unknown and addresses limitations of sampled distributed tracing for rare failures across Uber’s large service mesh. By Leela Kumili
infoqArticles.author: Leela Kumili

infoqArticles.title: AI in Production: Panellists Highlight Silent Failures, Harness Engineering, and Agent Governance
infoqArticles.description: A recent InfoQ webinar examined operational challenges in deploying agentic systems. Key points included issues like semantic and embedding drift, which can lead to significant errors. Experts discussed the need for automated code reviews, continuous evaluation of models, and enhanced privacy measures. The session emphasised a strategic approach to deployment and security management. By Olimpiu Po
infoqArticles.author: Olimpiu Pop

infoqArticles.title: Grafana Applies SLOs and Error Budgets to AI Agent Behaviour
infoqArticles.description: Grafana Labs is proposing a familiar reliability engineering approach for one of the less familiar problems in modern software: how to measure whether an AI agent is actually behaving well. By Craig Risi
infoqArticles.author: Craig Risi

infoqArticles.title: Mini book: Evolutionary Architecture in Practice
infoqArticles.description: Discover how to keep software evolvable as systems, technology, and teams shift. This edition explores agentic fitness functions for semantic drift, treating human comprehension as a core design metric, cross-cloud guardrails for regional autonomy, and aligning technical boundaries with Conway’s Law. Move beyond static diagrams to continuous feedback systems that keep change safe and intentional.
infoqArticles.author: InfoQ

infoqArticles.title: Helidon 27 Introduces Restructured Programming Models and New Messaging and Data Modules
infoqArticles.description: The release of Helidon 27 is the first release that follows the Oracle Tip & Tail Model of Library Development by which the Tip adopts the latest Java technology while the Tail provides a more stable and secure baseline. Concurrent with the release of JDK 27, new features in Helidon 27 include: an introduction to new major modules, Helidon Messaging and Helidon Data JDBC. By Michael Redlich
infoqArticles.author: Michael Redlich

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: Exploding GPUs
infoqArticles.description: Andrew Martin discusses why AI security is fundamentally tied to Kubernetes security. He shares insights into the evolving AI threat landscape, covering non-deterministic agent behavior, GPU supply chain vulnerabilities, shared compute risks, and practical defense strategies - from prompt firewalling to agentic identity - to help secure cloud-native AI workloads in production environments. By Andr
infoqArticles.author: Andrew Martin

infoqArticles.title: AWS Introduces Strands Decider 2B and Strands Box for AI Agent Development
infoqArticles.description: AWS has introduced two open-source projects for AI agent development: Strands Decider 2B, a small model designed to make decisions within agent workflows, and Strands Box, a sandbox for controlling agent execution. Both projects address different aspects of building agents that use tools, execute code, and interact with external systems. By Daniel Dominguez
infoqArticles.author: Daniel Dominguez

infoqArticles.title: Article: Cryptographic Foundation of Mobile ID Systems: An ISO/IEC 18013-5 Enterprise Architecture Blueprint
infoqArticles.description: This article provides a framework for asking the right architectural questions before an enterprise commits to an mDL provider or library. It shows which components can be abstracted safely, which trust boundaries must remain visible to the enterprise, what cryptographic and interoperability properties should be verified, and how requirements change across real-world use cases. By Praveen Kumar Go
infoqArticles.author: Praveen Kumar Gopalakrishnan

infoqArticles.title: Chainguard Launches Secure Workspaces and Checks for AI Coding Agents
infoqArticles.description: Software supply chain security company Chainguard has announced two beta products for running and testing code written by developers and AI agents. Chainguard Workspaces provides remote development environments based on hardened microVMs, while Chainguard Checks moves continuous integration into the development loop. The company announced both products at its Assemble London event. By Matt Saunder
infoqArticles.author: Matt Saunders

infoqArticles.title: Microsoft Commits Maia to Multi-Gigawatt Inference, and Its Efficiency Metric Draws Questions
infoqArticles.description: Microsoft will scale its Maia accelerator family to multi-gigawatt deployments from 2027, making it the primary inference system for its own products. Maia 300 collapses scale-up and scale-out onto one Ethernet fabric and moves KV state between prefill and decode workers without leaving it. Practitioners have questioned the tokens-per-watt claim that leads the announcement. By Steef-Jan Wiggers
infoqArticles.author: Steef-Jan Wiggers

infoqArticles.title: Instagram Modernized its UI with an AI-Native Architecture, Cutting Token Costs by 33%
infoqArticles.description: Instagram Direct migrated its Android UI from the legacy Android View system to Jetpack Compose, creating an AI-native UI codebase that is easier for AI coding agents to understand, modify, and maintain. According to Instagram engineers, the migration reduced UI code volume by 50% and token costs per AI agent session by 33%. By Sergio De Simone
infoqArticles.author: Sergio De Simone

infoqArticles.title: Optimizing Software Workflow: Exploring Fundamental Impacts in Technology
infoqArticles.description: Software only has value when shipped; faster release cadence matters. Development, deployment, and operations require different thinking, metrics, and investments. There are four impacts in tech: product success, compute capacity, engineering capacity, and strategic innovation. The biggest expense is people. AI shifts engineers toward deeper problem understanding, not fewer engineers. By Ben Linde
infoqArticles.author: Ben Linders

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: What 25 Trillion Tokens Reveal About How Developers Actually Adopt AI Agents
infoqArticles.description: Brendan O'Leary discusses how real-world AI adoption depends on building trust rather than chasing model benchmarks. Drawing from 40 trillion tokens of usage data, he explains the four rungs of the AI adoption ladder and analyzes key failure points in context construction, multi-model routing, and feedback loops to help engineering leaders successfully scale agentic workflows. By Brendan O’Leary
infoqArticles.author: Brendan O’Leary

infoqArticles.title: Grafana Tempo 3.1 Adds Query-Based Trace Redaction and Sampling-Aware TraceQL Metrics
infoqArticles.description: Grafana Labs has released Tempo 3.1, the first minor update to the 3.0 architecture. It adds TLS and additional SASL mechanisms to the Kafka client, lets operators redact traces with a TraceQL query instead of a list of trace IDs, and introduces an experimental query-time hint that corrects TraceQL metrics for sampled data. By Claudio Masolo
infoqArticles.author: Claudio Masolo
